source.title: Stochastic Modified Equations and Dynamics of Dropout Algorithm
source.authors: Zhongwang Zhang; Yuqing Li; Tao Luo; Z. Xu

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study empirically measures dropout-noise variance against loss-landscape flatness and Hessian curvature, using measures different from the claim versions’ specified generalization-gap measures.
record.gate_note: The reported noise-variance/flatness and Hessian-variance relationships are the study’s own measurements. They do not measure train-test gaps or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7, so the rows fit no listed version. Cited results about dropout’s generalization benefits are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures dropout-noise covariance and loss geometry, not any listed version's generalization outcome. It reports neither dropout-versus-control held-out error for V6 nor magnitude-aware sharpness versus train-test gaps for V7. Its generalization interpretation is inferred from these geometric relationships.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate but omits the stochastic modified equations. The authors derive weak approximations to two-layer dropout dynamics and empirically report inverse variance-flatness and Hessian-variance alignment relationships. They interpret these relationships as explaining a tendency toward flatter minima and improved generalization; they do not directly measure improved held-out performance.
record.recipe_differences: Studies dropout noise structure and loss geometry rather than the claim versions’ specified memorization, generalization-gap, or example-removal tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports measurements under different dropout probabilities, learning rates, network structures, datasets, and parameter versus gradient sampling; it notes distinct linear structure for gradient sampling compared with parameter sampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout-induced variance is larger along sharper directions, and projected variance correlates positively with Hessian eigenvalues in the tested FNN, ResNet-20, and Transformer settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout noise aligns with local loss curvature across the tested architectures and sampling methods.

record.problems: The study does not measure train-test error gaps. Several extended-experiment outcomes are shown only in figures, and the authors note a computational limitation on the isotropic-noise trace calculation.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for isotropic-noise trace comparisons: the prose reports this as a comparator within the Hessian-variance alignment result, not a separate claim-version outcome. No rows for training/test performance or cited prior findings because this study does not report them as its own measured results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including small-data, excessive-dropout, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The isotropic-noise trace comparison is explicitly declared in rows_left_out and requires no missing entry. The supplied manuscript identifies itself as a preprint under review, so the record's ICLR 2023 publication assertion is unsupported. Row states indicate inability to determine a listed claim version, not absence of the reported geometric relationships.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Dropout’s effect on held-out error across the specified regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and their relationship to train-test gaps; the study instead measures dropout-noise variance against loss flatness and Hessian curvature.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: FNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared dropout-noise variance with interval flatness using parameter trajectories and random gradients.

conditions.value: MNIST; first 10000 examples as training dataset

rows.measure: Relationship between PCA noise variance and interval flatness; authors report an inverse relationship and a power-law relationship.
rows.value: The text reports an inverse relationship; the figure gives approximate slopes of 2.3 for parameter data and 0.73 for gradient data.
rows.note: The paper reports the relationship in prose; precise per-setting values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported inverse variance-flatness relationship cannot establish any listed version. Appendix A restricts measurement to the weights and biases between the two hidden layers, rather than the entire FNN. Sampling occurs near a minimum with nearly 100% training accuracy. Here p denotes retention probability, not the fraction dropped; the reported slope magnitudes should not imply a positive variance-flatness relationship.

rows.subject: FNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian eigenvalues with projected dropout-noise variance using parameter trajectories and random gradients.

conditions.value: MNIST; first 10000 examples as training dataset

rows.measure: Relationship between Hessian eigenvalues and projected noise variance; authors report a consistent power-law relationship.
rows.value: The text reports a positive correlation; the figure gives approximate slopes of 1.3 for parameter data and 1 for gradient data.
rows.note: The paper reports the relationship in prose; precise per-setting values are figure-only.
rows.check: The positive curvature-noise relationship is reported, but cannot establish V7 without magnitude-aware perturbations and generalization gaps. Measurement concerns the selected hidden-layer parameters near the end of training; p is retention probability.

relation.reason: The authors interpret noise-geometry relationships as explaining improved generalization, without measuring dropout-versus-control held-out error or magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps.

tranche.reason: The study measures dropout-noise covariance and loss geometry. It neither tests a listed version's generalization outcome nor uses that finding as a tool.

source_check.notes: Measurements concern selected parameter matrices: the FNN's inter-hidden-layer weights and biases, ResNet's first convolution in its first block, and the transformer's first decoder block query projection. The parameter p is retention probability; Figure 3's caption explicitly states the qualitative inverse variance-flatness relationship.
